Pedosphere Scientific Classes

This reference covers all 24 certificate-backed scientific classes in relic.scientific.pedosphere: 24 executable concrete Functors, 0 fail-closed unavailable boundaries, and 0 abstract contracts. Each entry is generated from the live class, its IPHS certificate, State Contract Model, and ParameterManager metadata. Fail-closed unavailable classes are not instantiated during documentation generation.

The tables distinguish constructor controls, runtime variables, and ParameterManager scientific parameters. Values shown as package defaults belong to the documented RELIC architecture version and must not be copied as hardcoded constants into scientific code.

Certificate wildcard parameter groups (*, <pft>) are expanded to their exact current YAML entries. Every other declared parameter is matched to the parameter database by its exact full key; a declared name is never mapped to a key that merely ends with the same name.

Exact ParameterManager rows report the live YAML value, bounds, gradient policy, description, and provenance. A row whose value reads not declared in the parameter database is intentionally not assigned an invented default: the class metadata or certificate declares the quantity, with the meaning and units it states, but the parameter database has no key of that exact name.

IPHS levels are read from the sole certificate owner. Levels 1 to 3 describe compatibility, wrapping, or declared structure; they are not strict IPHS/GENERIC claims.

The Channel column of each runtime output contract applies relic.core.state.types.partition_outputs, the only runtime output channel classifier, to the declared output name. A name that the classifier reserves for diagnostics, such as diagnostics.*, goes to the diagnostics channel and is never committed as state. For any other name the channel is decided at run time by the write mode of the returned value: StateWriteMode.DERIVED routes the output to the diagnostics channel, and any other write mode sends it to the StateManager commit (a value without a write mode takes the run’s semantic-mode rules or the StateManager schema). The generator does not run forward(), so it does not predict that write mode. The Kind column is the State Contract Model kind of the variable and does not set its channel.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(\frac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}t} = I + T \cdot K \cdot C - \operatorname{diag} ( K ) \cdot C\) with mass balance

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit five-pool compartment incidence map plus the open heterotrophic export; this level-2 wrapper is not strict stoichiometric evidence

r_h

ParameterManager-backed gross decay, transfer, boundary-input, and respiration rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

boundary_route

five declared pool input ports supply carbon and heterotrophic_respiration exports carbon

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

empirical external environmental modifier; no Hamiltonian effort is claimed

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with the compartment incidence matrix and rate vector evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

PoolsMatrix.forward evaluates the five net pool tendencies and open respiration export exactly once through advance_reaction_network, then uses the StateManager-representable increment (C + Delta_C_raw) - C for both UpdateItem values and the carbon ledger.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

The compartment incidence map is explicit level-2 runtime structure and is not evidence for Hamiltonian or GENERIC closure.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(\frac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}t} = - k ( T, \theta ) \cdot C\) with \(k ( T, \theta ) = k_{\mathrm{ref}} \cdot f_{T} ( T ) \cdot f_{\theta} ( \theta )\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

six-channel identity wrapper for five net pool tendencies and the heterotrophic export; this is level-2 wrapping, not strict stoichiometric evidence

r_h

ParameterManager-backed vector of five net pool tendencies and the heterotrophic respiration rate

boundary_route

metabolic_litter_input plus structural_litter_input is the declared carbon source and heterotrophic_respiration is the declared atmospheric export

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

empirical temperature, moisture, litter-quality, and texture drivers; no Hamiltonian effort is claimed

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with a six-channel identity wrapper evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

FirstOrderDecomposition.forward evaluates five net pool tendencies and heterotrophic respiration once through advance_reaction_network before emitting canonical outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

The identity \(N_{h}\) wrapper is explicit level-2 runtime structure and is not evidence for strict stoichiometry or free-energy closure.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ V = \frac{\mathrm{MIC}\,V_{\max}(T,\theta)\,[S]}{K_m(T)+\mathrm{MIC}} \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit five-row four-column carbon incidence map for three uptake channels and microbial turnover

r_h

ParameterManager-backed metabolic, structural, available-SOM, and microbial-turnover rate vector

C_h

carbon ledger \([ 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 ]\) validates \(C_{h} N_{h} = 0\) at runtime

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

three substrate stocks, microbial biomass, and the atmosphere-facing respiration port

effort_variable

empirical temperature, moisture, and substrate controls; no Hamiltonian effort is claimed

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with the explicit five-row four-column carbon incidence map

runtime_usage

MicrobialEnzymeDecomposition.forward evaluates three reverse Michaelis-Menten uptake rates and one microbial-turnover rate exactly once through advance_reaction_network.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

\(C_{h} = [ 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 , 1 ] \mathrm{validates} C_{h} N_{h} = 0\) before the StateManager-ready increments and respiration flux are emitted.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Fresh non-woody plant litter uses a CENTURY-style quality partition; paired dung C/N uses a ParameterManager-backed conservative two-active-pool projection of the RothC FYM 49/49 active split.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(y_{h} = C_{h} x_{h}\) with element-preserving unit projection and \(F_{\mathrm{met}}\) + \(F_{\mathrm{str}} = F_{\mathrm{plant},C,g} + F_{\mathrm{dung},C,g}\), \(F_{\mathrm{organic},N} = F_{\mathrm{plant},N,g} + F_{\mathrm{dung},N,g}\)

Entry

Meaning

C_h

element-preserving sum, central kg-to-g unit projection, and conservative carbon partition

H_h

no thermodynamic metric is asserted for this level 2 boundary adapter

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

four required phenology element boundary fluxes, one dimensionless litter-quality control, and a dependency-selected grazing dung C/N pair

effort_variable

no thermodynamic effort is asserted for this level 2 port adapter

state_advancer

no stock is advanced; the runtime publishes three instantaneous target-side boundary ports

runtime_usage

LitterfallInterfaceMapper.forward requires finite non-negative tensors, makes the dung pair mandatory only when grazing_management is declared, rejects undeclared dung ports, delegates kg-to-g conversion to UnitConverter, and returns exactly three explicit REPLACE UpdateItems.

Composition channels and executable PortSpec API

Certificate composition channels: phenology_litterfall_boundary, grazing_dung_boundary, pedosphere_litter_carbon_input, pedosphere_litter_nitrogen_input

This class does not expose a class-level executable ports() schema. Certificate channels therefore describe composition evidence, not an instantiated PortSpec API. Metadata dependencies: no direct dependency list is declared; composition uses ports, owners, or graph wiring.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Yue et al. (2024) Eq. 33 gives \(\frac{\mathrm{d}M}{\mathrm{d}t} = P - O - E - D - T\), with atmospheric emission equal to the sum of top-layer transport mechanisms.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \mathrm{d}M_{\mathrm{raw}} = \mathrm{d}t \cdot ( T_{\mathrm{prod}} + T_{\mathrm{oxid}} + T_{\mathrm{trans}} ); \mathrm{d}M = \max ( \mathrm{d}M_{\mathrm{raw}} , - M ); R_{\mathrm{limit}} = ( \mathrm{d}M - \mathrm{d}M_{\mathrm{raw}} ) / \mathrm{d}t; F_{\mathrm{atm}} = F_{\mathrm{transport}} - R_{\mathrm{limit}} \]

Entry

Meaning

port_aggregation

one discrete aggregation of the three declared storage tendencies

storage_limiter

\(\mathrm{d}M = \max ( \mathrm{d}t \cdot ( T_{\mathrm{prod}} + T_{\mathrm{oxid}} + T_{\mathrm{trans}} ) , - M )\)

boundary_route

\(F_{\mathrm{atm}} = F_{\mathrm{transport}} - R_{\mathrm{limit}}\)

strict_structure_boundary

No H, effort, J, M, port-power, or GENERIC operator is claimed.

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

extensive soil methane-carbon storage and signed atmospheric boundary flux

effort_variable

No thermodynamic effort is asserted; the module consumes process rates and tendencies from declared scheduler dependencies.

state_advancer

one bounded explicit storage increment dM and one realized atmospheric boundary flux \(F_{\mathrm{atm}}\)

runtime_usage

MethaneBudgetCoupler.forward aggregates the declared tendencies once and returns the storage delta through UpdateItem ACCUMULATE with per_timestep true.

(2013) Eq. 19.1), \(F = 1 \mathrm{in} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{saturated} \mathrm{layer}\), and demand scaling to the available storage (Riley et al. (2011) Sect. 2.1.7).

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(N_{h} = [ [ 1 ] , [ - 1 ] ]\) and \(r_{h}\) equal to the storage-limited methane oxidation rate

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit \(\mathrm{stoichiometric}_{N} = [ [ 1 ] , [ - 1 ] ]\) mapping \(r_{h}\) to the oxidation export and negative storage tendency

r_h

ParameterManager-backed nonnegative methane oxidation rate evaluated by the canonical forward path

strict_structure_boundary

No independent H, effort, J, M, port-power, or GENERIC operator is claimed

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

methane oxidation export and its equal negative soil-storage tendency on the CH4-C basis

effort_variable

No thermodynamic effort is asserted; temperature, methane and oxygen concentrations are kinetic rate drivers.

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with \(N_{h} = [ [ 1 ] , [ - 1 ] ]\) and a single storage-limited oxidation rate \(r_{h}\)

runtime_usage

MethaneOxidationFunctor.forward calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting the four canonical outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

MethaneOxidationFunctor.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(P_{\mathrm{iMAPLE}} = \mathrm{Rh} r f_{\mathrm{ST}} f_{\mathrm{pH}} f_{\mathrm{wet}} ( \mathrm{Yue} \mathrm{et} \mathrm{al} . ( 2024 ) \mathrm{Eq} . 34 )\) with \(f_{\mathrm{ST}}\) from Yue et al. (2024) Eqs. 35-38 (Zhu et al. (2014) Eqs. 3-5 with the temperature-dependent Q10 of Yue et al. (2024) Eq. 39, \(\mathrm{Q}_{10} = \operatorname{clip} ( r_{b} Q_{b} ^ ( ( \mathrm{Ts} - T_{\mathrm{base}} ) / 10 ) , 1.7 , 16 ) , r_{b} = 3.0 , Q_{b} = 1.33 , T_{\mathrm{base}} = 25 C ; \mathrm{the} \operatorname{clip} \mathrm{is} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{observed} \mathrm{range} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{Zhu} \mathrm{et} \mathrm{al} . ( 2014 ) \mathrm{applied} \mathrm{in} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{released} \mathrm{iMAPLE} \mathrm{code} )\), \(f_{\mathrm{pH}}\) from Zhu et al. (2014) Eq. 6, and \(f_{\mathrm{wet}}\) the continuous inundation fraction; no closure factor multiplies Eq. 34. The calibrated branch Rh r \(f_{T}\) \(f_{\mathrm{Eh}}\) A (the same Zhu et al. (2014) peak \(f_{T}\), and the DNDC95 microbial activity index A in [0, 1]) and the blend weight are RELIC conventions with DNDC-type temperature and redox controls, not the DNDC substrate-kinetic model (Fumoto et al. 2008; van Bodegom and Scholten 2001), which is not implemented; its redox factor \(f_{\mathrm{Eh}}\) is the piecewise-linear form of Zhu et al. (2014) Sect. 2.2.1 after Zhang et al. (2002).

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Anaerobic nitrate reduction with Michaelis-Menten substrate limitation, carbon limitation, Q10 temperature response, a water-filled pore space anaerobic factor (DAYCENT basis, Del Grosso et al. 2000), pH response, and N2O:N2 product partitioning.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h} ( x_{h} , \theta ); x_{h} = [ \mathrm{NO}_{3} , \mathrm{N2O} , \mathrm{N}_{2} ] ^{\mathsf{T}} . \]

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit stoichiometric matrix in advance_reaction_network

r_h

denitrification rate split into N2O and N2 reaction channels

substrate_limiter

\(\min ( R_{\mathrm{den}} , \mathrm{NO}_{3} / \mathrm{d}t )\) applied before \(N_{h}\) \(r_{h}\)

time_integration

one explicit Euler step \(x ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) = x ( t ) + N_{h} r_{h} ( x ( t ) ) \mathrm{d}t \mathrm{per} \mathrm{governed} \mathrm{call}\) with the soil drivers held at their call-start values; simulator sub-steps repeat the step

sub_flow_accuracy

FunctorMetadata.sub_flow_accuracy ORDER_1 (Hairer, Norsett and Wanner 1993, Sect. II.3) while the donor limit is inactive, \(R_{\mathrm{den}} \mathrm{d}t < \mathrm{NO}_{3}\), i.e. Vmax \(f_{T} f_{\mathrm{anoxic}} f_{C} f_{\mathrm{pH}} \mathrm{d}t < K_m_{\mathrm{NO3}} + \mathrm{NO}_{3}\); binding on the two coarse grids of CR-A-04 T11 exhausts the numerical pool and yields equal final donor error, while smaller inactive-limit steps recover first order (a finite-step characterization, not loss of asymptotic convergence); the clipped N2O fraction only partitions the released nitrogen

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

nitrogen species cochain \(x_{h} = [ \mathrm{NO}_{3} , \mathrm{N2O} , \mathrm{N}_{2} ] ^{\mathsf{T}}\)

effort_variable

this required certificate slot records reaction-rate tensor \(r_{h}\) from ParameterManager-backed anaerobic kinetics; \(r_{h}\) is a rate vector and no thermodynamic effort is asserted

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit \(N_{h}\) and \(r_{h}\) evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

DenitrificationProcess.forward calls advance_reaction_network before emitting NO3, N2O, and N2 outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

DenitrificationProcess.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

pedosphere.physical.wfps_denitrification_threshold

dimensionless

0.6; bounds=(0.5, 0.8)

fixed

Water-filled pore space WFPS_thr above which the denitrification anaerobic factor rises, f_anoxic = max(clip((WFPS - WFPS_thr)/w, 0, 1), f_min) with w = pedosphere.denitrification.anaerobic_transition_width and f_min = pedosphere.denitrification.minimum_anaerobic_factor. Linn and Doran (1984) found aerobic microbial activity maximal at 60 percent WFPS and declining above it through reduced aeration; DAYCENT (Del Grosso et al. 2000) drives denitrification with WFPS. Bounds: nitrification is the main N2O source up to 60 percent and denitrification produced all N2O at 70 percent WFPS (Bateman and Baggs 2005); 0.8 keeps the ramp inside the unit interval.

Source: literature; Linn, D.M. and Doran, J.W. (1984) Effect of water-filled pore space on carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide production in tilled and nontilled soils, Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 48, 1267-1272, doi:10.2136/sssaj1984.03615995004800060013x; Del Grosso, S.J., Parton, W.J., Mosier, A.R., Ojima, D.S., Kulmala, A.E. and Phongpan, S. (2000) General model for N2O and N2 gas emissions from soils due to dentrification, Global Biogeochem. Cycles 14, 1045-1060, doi:10.1029/1999GB001225

pedosphere.denitrification.anaerobic_transition_width

dimensionless

0.3; bounds=(0.1, 0.5)

learnable

Width w, in water-filled pore space, of the linear rise of the denitrification anaerobic factor from WFPS_thr to WFPS_thr + w (0.6 to 0.9 with the defaults), f_anoxic = max(clip((WFPS - WFPS_thr)/w, 0, 1), f_min).

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (width of the linear WFPS ramp; no literature value)

pedosphere.denitrification.minimum_anaerobic_factor

dimensionless

0.1; bounds=(0.01, 0.3)

learnable

Floor f_min of the denitrification anaerobic factor at low water-filled pore space (anaerobic microsites), f_anoxic = max(clip((WFPS - WFPS_thr)/w, 0, 1), f_min).

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (anaerobic factor floor; no literature value)

pedosphere.denitrification.ph_minimum_factor

dimensionless

0.2; bounds=(0.1, 0.5)

learnable

Minimum pH response factor

Source: pH tolerance range; pH tolerance range

pedosphere.denitrification.min_rate_threshold

dimensionless

1e-12; bounds=(0.0, inf)

fixed

Lower bound of the denitrification temperature factor f_T = clip(Q10^((T - T_ref)/10), lower, upper) with Q10 = q10_denitrification and T_ref = reference_temperature. With the default Q10 = 2.2 and T_ref = 293.15 K the raw factor reaches 1e-12 only 350 K below T_ref, so the bound never binds at a physical soil temperature; it keeps f_T strictly positive. A floor of the temperature response factor cannot be negative; its upper limit is max_rate_factor, a relation between parameters that bounds cannot express, so the upper bound is open (inf).

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (temperature factor lower bound; no literature value)

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Michaelis-Menten ammonia oxidation with Q10, water-filled pore space oxygen (Linn and Doran 1984), and pH modifiers; N2O is a fixed fraction of nitrified nitrogen.

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h} ( x_{h} , \theta ); x_{h} = [ \mathrm{NH}_{4} , \mathrm{NO}_{3} , \mathrm{N2O} ] ^{\mathsf{T}} . \]

Entry

Meaning

N_h

explicit stoichiometric matrix in advance_reaction_network

r_h

Michaelis-Menten nitrification rate split into NO3 and N2O reaction channels

substrate_limiter

\(\min ( R_{\mathrm{nit}} , \mathrm{NH}_{4} / \mathrm{d}t )\) applied before \(N_{h}\) \(r_{h}\)

time_integration

one explicit Euler step \(x ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) = x ( t ) + N_{h} r_{h} ( x ( t ) ) \mathrm{d}t \mathrm{per} \mathrm{governed} \mathrm{call}\) with the soil drivers held at their call-start values; simulator sub-steps repeat the step

sub_flow_accuracy

FunctorMetadata.sub_flow_accuracy ORDER_1 (Hairer, Norsett and Wanner 1993, Sect. II.3) while the donor limit is inactive, \(R_{\mathrm{nit}} \mathrm{d}t < \mathrm{NH}_{4}\), i.e. Vmax \(f_{T} f_{\mathrm{O2}} f_{\mathrm{pH}} \mathrm{d}t < K_m + \mathrm{NH}_{4}\); binding on the two coarse grids of CR-A-04 T11 exhausts the numerical pool and yields equal final donor error, while smaller inactive-limit steps recover first order (a finite-step characterization, not a loss of asymptotic convergence)

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

nitrogen species cochain \(x_{h} = [ \mathrm{NH}_{4} , \mathrm{NO}_{3} , \mathrm{N2O} ] ^{\mathsf{T}}\)

effort_variable

this required certificate slot records reaction-rate tensor \(r_{h}\) from ParameterManager-backed kinetics; \(r_{h}\) is a rate vector and no thermodynamic effort is asserted

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit \(N_{h}\) and \(r_{h}\) evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

NitrificationProcess.forward calls advance_reaction_network before emitting NH4, NO3, and N2O outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

NitrificationProcess.forward materializes stoichiometric_N and rates, then lowers \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

pedosphere.nitrification.km_nh4

g N m-2

0.005; bounds=(0.001, 0.02)

learnable

Areal NH4 half-saturation constant Km of the RELIC nitrification rate R = Vmax NH4/(Km + NH4) f_T f_O2 f_pH.

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (areal NH4 half-saturation; no literature value)

pedosphere.physical.wfps_nitrification_optimum

dimensionless

0.6; bounds=(0.35, 0.7)

learnable

Water-filled pore space WFPS_opt at which aerobic microbial activity, and with it nitrification, peaks; above it oxygen limits nitrification, f_O2 = max((1 - WFPS)/(1 - WFPS_opt), pedosphere.nitrification.minimum_oxygen_factor), and below it f_O2 = 1. Linn and Doran (1984) found the maximum at 60 percent WFPS with a decline above it through reduced aeration. The bounds are the Bateman and Baggs (2005) range: nitrification is the main N2O source at 35-60 percent WFPS and denitrification produced all N2O at 70 percent.

Source: literature; Linn, D.M. and Doran, J.W. (1984) Effect of water-filled pore space on carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide production in tilled and nontilled soils, Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 48, 1267-1272, doi:10.2136/sssaj1984.03615995004800060013x; Bateman, E.J. and Baggs, E.M. (2005) Contributions of nitrification and denitrification to N2O emissions from soils at different water-filled pore space, Biol. Fertil. Soils 41, 379-388, doi:10.1007/s00374-005-0858-3

pedosphere.nitrification.minimum_oxygen_factor

dimensionless

0.1; bounds=(0.01, 0.3)

learnable

Floor of the dimensionless nitrification oxygen response factor, f_O2 = max((1 - WFPS)/(1 - WFPS_opt), f_O2_min) above WFPS_opt = pedosphere.physical.wfps_nitrification_optimum; with the default 0.1 and 0.6 it binds only for WFPS > 0.96.

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (oxygen response factor floor; no literature value)

pedosphere.nitrification.temperature_maximum

K

323.15; bounds=(0.0, inf)

fixed

Upper soil temperature limit of the nitrification temperature factor (50 degC): above it f_T is multiplied by extreme_temperature_factor. An absolute (thermodynamic) temperature in K cannot be negative; the lower bound is 0 K.

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (temperature factor upper limit; no literature value)

pedosphere.nitrification.ph_minimum_factor

dimensionless

0.1; bounds=(0.01, 0.3)

learnable

Floor of the nitrification pH response factor f_pH = clip(exp(-0.5 ((pH - pH_opt)/w_pH)^2), ph_minimum_factor, 1).

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (pH response factor floor; no literature value)

pedosphere.nitrification.min_rate_threshold

dimensionless

0.001; bounds=(0.0, inf)

fixed

Lower bound of the nitrification temperature factor f_T = clip(Q10^((T - T_ref)/10) * f_extreme, lower, upper). With the default parameters it binds only below temperature_minimum (273.15 K), where it holds f_T at 0.001. A floor of the temperature response factor cannot be negative; its upper limit is max_rate_factor, a relation between parameters that bounds cannot express, so the upper bound is open (inf).

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (temperature factor lower bound; no literature value)

pedosphere.nitrification.max_rate_factor

dimensionless

10.0; bounds=(1.0, 100.0)

fixed

Upper bound of the nitrification temperature factor f_T. With the default parameters it never binds (f_T <= 8 at 323.15 K, and 0.001 times the Q10 term above it), so it is a protective bound; it binds inside the range only when Q10^((T_max - T_ref)/10) > 10, for example Q10 = 2.5 above about 318.3 K.

Source: relic_convention; RELIC convention value (temperature factor upper bound; no literature value)

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{NH}_{4}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mathrm{mineralization} - \mathrm{nitrification} - \mathrm{uptake}_{\mathrm{NH4}}; \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{NO}_{3}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mathrm{nitrification} - \mathrm{denitrification} - \mathrm{leaching} - \mathrm{uptake}_{\mathrm{NO3}} \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

diagnostic \(\dot{d} = N_{h} r_{h}\) for dependency increments; prognostic \(\Delta_{\mathrm{NH4},\mathrm{ext}} = c_{\mathrm{kg},\mathrm{to},g} ( F_{\mathrm{fert}} + F_{\mathrm{urine}} ) \mathrm{d}t\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

declared stoichiometric or output incidence map for this reaction process

r_h

ParameterManager-backed process-rate vector evaluated by the production forward path

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

ammonium and nitrate dependency increments in g N m-2

effort_variable

already evaluated child-process increments supplied by the dependency graph

state_advancer

\(\dot{d} = N_{h} r_{h}\) is evaluated only as a diagnostic projection; the aggregate fertilizer and selected-urine boundary supplies the sole StateManager increment

runtime_usage

NitrogenCycling.forward calls advance_reaction_network with explicit \(N_{h}\) and \(r_{h}\) under diagnostic_residual routing, never re-emits child state or flux outputs, and emits only the aggregate external NH4 increment.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

NitrogenCycling.forward materializes the two-row mineral-N diagnostic incidence map and evaluates \(N_{h}\) \(r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ U = V_{\max} \cdot C / ( K_m + C ) \cdot f_{T} \cdot f_{W} \cdot W_{\mathrm{root}} \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x}=N_h r_h \]

with ParameterManager-backed process rates \(r_h\) and declared stoichiometric/output map \(N_h\)

Entry

Meaning

N_h

three signed transfer columns map nitrate and ammonium to plant N and soil P to plant P

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

declared RELIC state, port, or observation cochain basis

effort_variable

ParameterManager-backed thermodynamic effort, driver, or diagnostic input used by the module

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) with explicit stoichiometric_N and rates evaluated by advance_reaction_network

runtime_usage

RootNutrientUptake.forward calls advance_reaction_network with declared stoichiometric_N and rates before emitting canonical outputs.

explicit_stoichiometric_usage

RootNutrientUptake.forward materializes nitrate, ammonium, and phosphate transfer columns and validates equivalent-mole N plus mass-basis P ledgers before lowering \(\dot{x} = N_{h} r_{h}\) through advance_reaction_network.

layered_donor_increments

donor pools declared with a layer axis receive per-layer increments \(\Delta_{\mathrm{pool}} ( z ) = - M U ( z ) \mathrm{d}t\) whose layer sum equals the areal \(N_{h}\) \(r_{h}\) dt transfer; plant_n_storage and plant_p_storage receive the areal increment, so StateManager shapes match the declared pool shapes

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Freundlich equilibrium sorption with retardation (Jury and Horton 2004; Mayes et al. 2012) and first-order dissolved-phase degradation; semi-explicit index-1 DAE with algebraic elimination (Hairer and Wanner 1996)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(E \dot{x} = f ( x )\), \(g ( x ) = 0\) with \(x = ( y , C , S )\), \(E = \operatorname{diag} ( 1 , 0 , 0 )\), \(g = ( \theta C + \rho_{b} S - y , S - K_{f} C ^ n )\); \(g_{z}\) invertible (index 1)

Entry

Meaning

constraint

\(g ( y , C ) = \theta C + \rho_{b} K_{f} C ^ n - y\) with \(g_{C} = \theta + \rho_{b} K_{f} n C ^ ( n - 1 ) > 0 ( \mathrm{index} 1 )\)

elimination

scalar monotone equation \(F ( C ' ) = \theta C ' + \rho_{b} K_{f} C ' ^ n + \mathrm{d}t \lambda \theta C ' - y \mathrm{solved}\) on the exact bracket [0, y/theta] by the existing BracketedBisectionSolver

differential_update

implicit Euler y’ = y - dt lambda theta C’

restart_projection

the stored (y, C, S) triple is re-verified for consistency at every step, so a restored checkpoint is re-projected by the same check before advancing

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

differential total mass y on the cell basis with the algebraic pair (C, S) on the constraint manifold; no storage functional is claimed

effort_variable

none; the partition and isotherm are algebraic constraints, not variational efforts

state_advancer

y’ = y - dt lambda theta C’ with C’ from the bracketed solve of the implicit constraint and S’ = \(K_{f}\) C’^n

runtime_usage

EquilibriumSorptionFunctor.forward validates states and water content, rejects inconsistent triples, solves the scalar constraint with BracketedBisectionSolver, raises on non-convergence, emits one ACCUMULATE increment, two REPLACE algebraic states, and three REPLACE diagnostics, and reports the total-mass ledger residual through check_conservation_laws.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ J_z = - \mathrm{Deff} \frac{\partial C}{\partial z}; F_{\mathrm{surface},\mathrm{out}} = - J_z ( 0 ) \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{c} = - D_{h} q_{h} + G_{h} u_{h}, q_{h} = - \star_{K} D_{h} ^{\mathsf{T}} e_{h}, e_{h} = \delta H_{h} / \delta c_{h} \]

Entry

Meaning

D_h

existing gradient and flux-divergence operator used by forward()

star_K

HodgeStarSpec assembled from ParameterManager-backed CO2 and N2O effective diffusivities

q_h

soil gas diffusive flux cochain computed by Fick law

G_h

soil-atmosphere CO2 and N2O matter-port map

H_h

quadratic concentration storage \(H_{h} = 0.5 \cdot c_{h}^{\mathsf{T}} c_{h}\)

sigma_h

non-negative diffusion dissipation \(X_{h}^{\mathsf{T}} \star_{K} X_{h}\)

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

CO2 and N2O layer concentrations are declared as primal 0-cochains on pedosphere_soil_gas_diffusion

effort_variable

\(e_{h} = \delta H_{h} / \delta c_{h} = c_{h}\) for stacked CO2 and N2O concentration cochains

state_advancer

\(\delta C_{\mathrm{raw},i} = - ( J_{i} + 1 / 2 - J_{i} - 1 / 2 ) \frac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}z}\) with \(F_{\mathrm{surface},\mathrm{out}} = - J_{\mathrm{top}}\) and \(J_{\mathrm{bottom}} = 0\); \(\delta C_{\mathrm{accepted},i} = \max ( - C_{i} , \delta C_{\mathrm{raw},i} )\)

runtime_usage

GasDiffusion1D.forward computes ParameterManager-backed effective diffusivity once, advances each exact-grid concentration through one conservative finite-volume divergence, and returns explicit UpdateItems plus signed species-specific clipping routes.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\[ ALE conservation form with relative flux F - c w (Donea et al. 2004) and the discrete geometric conservation law V_i(t+dt) = V_i(t) + dt (w_{i+1/2} - w_{i-1/2}) (Thomas and Lombard 1979); Fickian diffusion (Crank 1975) \]

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(\dot{x} = - R_{h} e + f_{\mathrm{geo}} + s_{\mathrm{boundary}}\) with \(e = c\), \(R_{h} = d_{h} ^{\mathsf{T}} \operatorname{diag} ( D ) d_{h} / \mathrm{d}x ^ 2\), e^\(T f_{\mathrm{geo}} = - 0.5 c ^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot ( \mathrm{star} ) c\), \(\cdot ( \mathrm{star} ) = \operatorname{diag} ( w_{b} / N )\)

Entry

Meaning

diffusive_rate

canonical _compute_diffusion_rate_and_boundary_flux_1d with zero-flux closed faces on the current metric \(\mathrm{d}x = L / N\)

relative_flux

\(s_{k} = c_{\mathrm{face},k} w_{k}\) with the face concentration upwind of the face motion (\(c_{b}\) outside a growing boundary; bottom-cell value for a shrinking boundary)

geometric_conservation

\(V_i(t+dt) = L(t+dt)/N = V_i(t) + dt (w_{i+1} - w_i) exactly\) for the uniform stretching mapping

hodge_time_derivative

\(\cdot ( \mathrm{star} ) = \operatorname{diag} ( w_{b} / N )\) on the concentration cochain; the geometry power is emitted as a diagnostic

mapping

uniform stretching \(x = \mathrm{xi} L ( t )\); refinement, non-uniform mapping, and remap are [N]

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

concentration cochain c with metric \(\mathrm{star} = \operatorname{diag} ( L / N )\); storage \(H = 0.5 c ^{\mathsf{T}} \mathrm{star} c\)

effort_variable

\(e = c\)

state_advancer

\(m_i(t+dt) = m_i(t) + dt [rate_i dx + s_{i+1} - s_i]\), \(c_{i} ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) = m_{i} ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) / V_{i} ( t + \mathrm{d}t )\), \(L ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) = L + w_{b} \mathrm{d}t\)

runtime_usage

MovingDomainDiffusionFunctor.forward validates states, forcings, and the step, enforces the diffusion and mesh Courant limits, evaluates the diffusive rate with the canonical owner, adds the relative fluxes, emits two ACCUMULATE increments and four REPLACE diagnostics, and reports the column ledger residual through check_conservation_laws.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Mixed-form Richards water balance with Darcy flux \(q = - K ( \theta ) \nabla ( h + z )\) and storage tendency \(\frac{\mathrm{d}\theta}{\mathrm{d}t} = - \operatorname{div} ( q ) + S .\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{\theta} = - D_{h} q_{h} + G_{h} u_{h}; q_{h} = - \star_{K} d ( h + z ); u_{h} = ( \mathrm{infiltration}_{\mathrm{flux}} - \mathrm{evapotranspiration}_{\mathrm{flux}} ) / \mathrm{water}_{\mathrm{density}}; \star_{K} = \star_{K}^{\mathsf{T}} \geq 0 . \]

Entry

Meaning

D_h

existing one-dimensional finite-difference divergence used by the shared RichardsNumericalSolver modified-Picard correction

star_K

build_hodge_contract and build_hodge_terms HodgeStarSpec with saturated_conductivity

source_port

\(( \mathrm{infiltration}_{\mathrm{flux}} - \mathrm{evapotranspiration}_{\mathrm{flux}} ) / \mathrm{water}_{\mathrm{density}}\)

boundary_operator

one-dimensional Richards boundary handling with \(q_{\mathrm{bottom}} = K ( \theta_{\mathrm{bottom}} ) g_{z}\) for free drainage and explicit surface/drainage PortSpecIPHS declarations

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

cellwise volumetric-water-content profile theta_h; column storage is derived with dz

effort_variable

hydraulic-head gradient \(X_{h} = d ( h + z )\) with conductivity mobility star_K

state_advancer

\(\dot{\theta} = - D_{h} q_{h} + G_{h} u_{h}\); \(q_{h} = - \star_{K} X_{h}\)

runtime_usage

_compute_iphs_richards_state_update applies the shared canonical mixed-residual correction, accepts only configured residual or verified machine-precision convergence, and routes mass residual diagnostics.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

\(\frac{\partial(B C)}{\partial t} = -\frac{\partial J}{\partial z}\), \(B=\theta+\rho_bK_d\), \(K=\alpha_L\lvert q\rvert+D_w(T)\theta^{10/3}/\phi^2\)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\(B_{h} \dot{c}_{h} = - D_{h} J_{h} + G_{h} u_{h}\) with declared storage, solute flux, and top/bottom matter ports

Entry

Meaning

D_h

finite-volume incidence/divergence map on the nonuniform vertical grid

star_D

level-3 structural PSD Hodge initialized by the ParameterManager-backed default molecular diffusivity; the full runtime K coefficient is evaluated directly by forward()

q_h

\(J=qC_{upwind}-K\,\frac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}z}\) evaluated once at every finite-volume face

G_h

explicit top Cauchy input and bottom free-drainage export matter-port map

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

NO3 and DOC layer concentrations are declared as primal 0-cochains on pedosphere_solute_transport

effort_variable

The level 3 structural audit uses concentration cochains and a positive storage capacity B; it does not claim a thermodynamic effort or strict port-power pairing

state_advancer

\(B_iC_i^{n+1}=B_iC_i^n-\Delta t(J_{i+1/2}-J_{i-1/2})/\Delta z_i\) with explicit top and bottom ports

runtime_usage

SoluteAdvectionDiffusion1D.forward evaluates one nonuniform-grid finite-volume transport law with capacity-weighted CFL substeps; it contains no reaction branch, second operator path, or concentration fallback.

Governing equations and canonical operator

Literature or process form

Two-region mobile-immobile first-order mass transfer (van Genuchten and Wierenga 1976); multirate mass transfer memory function with exponential kernel (Haggerty and Gorelick 1995)

Canonical RELIC structural form

\[ \dot{x} = - R e, R = \alpha [ [ 1 , - 1 ] , [ - 1 , 1 ] ], e = \frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}x} = ( c_{m} , c_{\mathrm{im}} ), H = 0.5 ( \theta_{m} c_{m} ^ 2 + \theta_{\mathrm{im}} c_{\mathrm{im}} ^ 2 ) \]

Entry

Meaning

R_h

alpha [[1, -1], [-1, 1]] symmetric positive semidefinite dissipation on the effort pair (\(c_{m}\), \(c_{\mathrm{im}}\))

J_h

zero; the exchange is purely dissipative

memory_kernel

\(K ( t ) = \alpha \mathrm{omega} \exp ( - \mathrm{omega} t )\) with \(\mathrm{omega} = \alpha / \theta_{\mathrm{im}} \mathrm{obtained}\) by eliminating \(c_{\mathrm{im}}\); realization d eta/\(\mathrm{d}t = - \mathrm{omega} \eta + \mathrm{omega} c_{m}\) with \(\eta = c_{\mathrm{im}}\)

time_integration

exact matrix-exponential update of the linear exchange with coefficients constant during one call; governed T11 verifies the dt-halving ladder against an independent 2-by-2 matrix exponential and the semigroup under unequal partitions

sub_flow_accuracy

FunctorMetadata.sub_flow_accuracy EXACT for the concentration state update up to floating-point rounding; the step-start diagnostic rates are not time-integrated by this declaration; one fast member reports exact, while an interacting composition remains limited by its other sub-flows and composition order

State advancement, conservation, and open boundaries

Entry

Meaning

potential_basis

theta-weighted storage \(x = ( \theta_{m} c_{m} , \theta_{\mathrm{im}} c_{\mathrm{im}} )\) with \(H = 0.5 ( \theta_{m} c_{m} ^ 2 + \theta_{\mathrm{im}} c_{\mathrm{im}} ^ 2 )\)

effort_variable

\(e = \frac{\mathrm{d}H}{\mathrm{d}x} = ( c_{m} , c_{\mathrm{im}} )\)

state_advancer

\(\dot{x} = - R e \mathrm{realized} \mathrm{exactly} \mathrm{per} \mathrm{step}\) by \(d ( t + \mathrm{d}t ) = d ( t ) \exp ( - \kappa \mathrm{d}t )\) with the theta-weighted total held fixed

runtime_usage

TwoRegionMassTransferFunctor.forward validates both states and the step, evaluates the exact exchange, emits two ACCUMULATE increments and three REPLACE diagnostics, and reports the theta-weighted ledger residual through check_conservation_laws.
